Fixes #7660
## Brief summary
1. Run EprintCleanup on a copy of the entry the ArXiv fetcher is fetching before getting arXiv id from the eprint field;
2. Add two test method. One finds full text with title containing colon and journal, while another finds full text with title containing colon and url.

## Problem
When finding full text, this BibTeX reference works:
```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint        = {2002.10248},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```
![#7660-0](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48386227/115873907-13c97c80-a476-11eb-821f-24598bd1a8a9.png)

But when `eprint` field is missing, no full text will be found:
```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```
![#7660-1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48386227/115873922-188e3080-a476-11eb-80e7-222c58ee4e09.png)

## Solution
Since the title contains colon and arXiv uses colon to represent key and value, the title may be recognized mistakenly. So use other fields to get the eprint field to avoid this problem. Thanks to the advice from @tobiasdiez .

## Screenshots
After fix:
![#7660-2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/48386227/115873880-0f04c880-a476-11eb-9291-82e011f87ab3.png)

Title: Unable to download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing
Body: <!-- 
Note: Please use the GitHub issue tracker only for bug reports. 
Feature requests, questions and general feedback is now handled at http://discourse.jabref.org.
Thanks! 
--> 

JabRef version 5.3 developmental portable JAR 

<!-- IMPORTANT NOTE ->
<!-- 
      Please always test if the bug is still reproducible in the latest development version.
      We are constantly improving JabRef and some bugs may already be fixed.
      You can download the development version at: http://builds.jabref.org/main
      Please make a backup of your library before you try out this version.
      If you already use a development version, ensure that you use the latest one.
 -->
- [x ] **Mandatory**: I have tested the latest development version from http://builds.jabref.org/main and the problem persists

<!-- Add a clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

I am unable to automatically download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing. For example, this BibTeX reference works:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint        = {2002.10248},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

but this one doesn't:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

with the only thing different is the eprint field.

Interestingly this doesn't always happen; most of the time JabRef can fetch the arXiv PDF correctly without the eprint field, but for some reason JabRef fails to get other arXiv PDFs like the one above. I suspect it's a formatting issue similar to Issue #7633. It's not always consistent, but it feels like paper titles with colons appear to trigger this behavior more than others.

Perhaps it can be set when the url field is provided that JabRef could use that as a fallback to download the PDF..

Title: Add cleanup action: "Make LaTeX ready: Escape $"
Body: **Problem:**

1. Want to prepare entries to be used with LaTeX
2. Want to not start math-mode, but instead simply render `$` character in my bibliography

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Add cleanup action that adds a backslash in front of $
- Name this cleanup action: `Make LaTeX ready: Escape $`
- Add to the documentation: `Adds backslash to $ characters. \$ will be rendered by LaTeX as $ instead of starting math-mode. Do not use this cleanup action, if you have entries that require usage of LaTeX math-mode.`

**Additional context**
- Why not add this function to `Make LaTeX ready: Cleanup` or `Make LaTeX ready: Unicode to LaTeX`? Both allow the usage of math-mode, which is fine. This seems to be a zero-sum game and there is no heuristic that can find out if the user wants to use math-mode or simply render the $.

Related to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8490#issuecomment-1091209909 and #8650

Fix for Issue #3247

When JabRef was run with the '-n' parameter, i.e. the "No GUI" option, like:
`java -jar JabRef.jar -n`
or any other reason for `ArgumentProcessor#shouldShutDown()` returning `true` took place, the application should shut down after performing custom export filters etc. However, `Platform.exit()` wasn't called, so the JavaFX thread kept running indefinitely. Simply added this call to resolve the problem.

Title: Table of formatters
Body: This issue summarizes all the available formatters.
The aim is to improve their names and descriptions.
I think the most practicable way is to directly edit this post with the new proposed version.

| Class Name | Key | Name | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AuthorsFormatter | AuthorsFormatter | BibTex authors format | Normalizes lists of persons in %s to the BibTeX standard |
| UpperEachFirst CaseChanger | UpperEachFirst CaseChanger | Upper Each First | Converts the first character of each word in %s to upper case (and all others to lower case), but does not change words starting with "{". |
| UpperCaseChanger | UpperCaseChanger | UPPER | Converts all characters in %s to upper case, but does not change words starting with "{" |
| MonthFormatter | MonthFormatter | Month | Normalizes content of %s to the format #mon#. |
| LatexFormatter | LatexFormatter | Latex | Cleans latex code in %s. |
| UpperFirst CaseChanger | UpperFirst CaseChanger | Upper first | Converts the first character of the first word in %s to upper case (and the remaining characters of the first word to lower case), but does not change anything if word starts with "{". |
| AuthorsMinifier | MinifyAuthors | Minify authors | Replaces three or more authors with "and others". |
| DateFormatter | DateFormatter | Date | Normalizes dates in %s to the BibLaTeX standard yyyy-mm-dd or yyyy-mm. |
| TitleCaseChanger | TitleCaseChanger | Title | Converts all words in %s to upper case, but converts articles, prepositions, and conjunctions to lower case. |
| CaseKeeper | CaseKeeper | CaseKeeper | Adds {} brackets around acronyms, month names and countries in %s to preserve their case. |
| PageNumbers Formatter | PageNumbers Formatter | Page numbers | Ensures that pages numbers in %s are of the form num--num. |
| LowerCaseChanger | LowerCaseChanger | lower | Converts all characters in %s to lower case, but does not change words starting with "{" |
| TrimFormatter | TrimFormatter | Trim whitespace | Removes any leading and trailing whitespace in %s. |
| HTMLToLatex Formatter | HtmlConverter **HtmlToLatex** | HTMLConverter **HTML to LaTeX** | Changes HTML expressions in %s to their LaTeX equivalent. |
| SuperscriptFormatter | SuperscriptFormatter | Superscripts | Transforms ordinal numbers in %s into LaTex superscripts. |

Changes include modifications to the `BibTeXConverter`, `MSBibConverter`, and related classes to better manage the conversion process between BibTeX and MS Bib formats. issue_text:
Title: Export to MS Office 2007 (.xml) - Author is Company
Body: JabRef version 3.4 on Windows 10

When exporting to MS Office 2007 (.xml) names in curly braces should be treated as companies and exported as such.

In Section 2.3.3. of the manual of the biblatex package - which for me nowadays is the main reference of how to use bib files - it is given:
"Corporate authors and editors are given in the author or editor field, respectively. Note that they must be wrapped in an extra pair of curly braces to prevent data parsing from treating them as personal names which are to be dissected into their components."

MS Office also knows companies as authors and has the following syntax for it:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:Corporate>Basel Committee on Banking Supervision</b:Corporate>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

So it would be perfect if Jabref recognizes author names in curly braces and exports them as corporates. 

At the moment one gets the following result:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:NameList>
            <b:Person>
                <b:Last>Supervision</b:Last>
                <b:Middle>Committee on Banking</b:Middle>
                <b:First>Basel</b:First>
            </b:Person>
        </b:NameList>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

This then results in MS Word in the same incorrect presentation you would see when inputting the name without curly braces in the bib file and using it in a normal (la)tex document (so for the examle you would have "Supervision, Committee on Banking" or "Supervision, C. o. B").

By the way, I want to thank you for the extremely fast resolving of my MS Office export problem last week (#1485) and it would be very nice if you can get this new problem solved as well. (In fact, if you can do it, then I would like to ask if you could include this in the same build as for the last week problem, so that I can test them both together.)

I am unable to automatically download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing. For example, this BibTeX reference works:

  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},

I suspect it's a formatting issue similar to Issue #7633. It's not always consistent, but it feels like paper titles with colons appear to trigger this behavior more than others.

description_text: This pull request refactors the placement of parsing and writing logic to improve code organization and maintainability. The changes ensure that responsibilities are clearly separated, making the codebase easier to understand and modify.
issue_text:
Title: [Code] Placement of parsing and writing logic
Body: Right now parsing and serialization is not handled in a uniform way. (see e.g #875)

Possible designs which come to my mind:
- The BibParser and BibWriter contain all the logic as private methods.
  - e.g.: BibParser.parseMetaData(String stringyMetadata) and BibWriter.writeMetaData(Metadata)
  -  pro: encapsulation of responsibilities
  - contra: rather big classes BibParser and BibWriter, hard to test
- There are transformer classes which just convert the string to the object and vice-versa.
  - e.g.: MetadataTransformer with static parse(String stringyMetadata) and static write(Metadata) [suggestions for a better name then transformer? ReadWriter?]
  - pro: encapsulation of responsibilities (but weaker as 1), can be reused somewhere else, better testability
  - contra: exposes writing and parsing to the outside world, many new classes
- The corresponding objects have methods which allow parsing and converting to string.
  - e.g.: Metadata has static parse(String stringyMetadata) [or constructor?] and serialize()
  - pro: encapsulation of responsibilities (but weaker as 1 and 2), can be reused somewhere else, better testability as 1
  - contra: exposes writing and parsing to the outside world, scatters parsing and writing logic 

I have no strong opinion about which option we should use (slightly preferring 2), but we should decide for _one_ to handle parsing and writing uniformly.

dependencies {

Title: Unable to download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing

<!-- Add a clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

I am unable to automatically download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing. For example, this BibTeX reference works:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint        = {2002.10248},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

but this one doesn't:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

with the only thing different is the eprint field.

Interestingly this doesn't always happen; most of the time JabRef can fetch the arXiv PDF correctly without the eprint field, but for some reason JabRef fails to get other arXiv PDFs like the one above. I suspect it's a formatting issue similar to Issue #7633. It's not always consistent, but it feels like paper titles with colons appear to trigger this behavior more than others.

description_text:
Introduce explicit SpecialField model and migration to separate previously encoded special fields into dedicated fields

Summary
- Add SpecialField and SpecialFieldValue model types to represent application-defined special fields (e.g., read status, priority) and their allowed values.
- Implement a migration (SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields) that converts old encodings of special fields into separate fields when opening/upgrading a library.
- Update GUI to treat special fields as first-class fields: context menu actions, toolbar/menu actions, labels and icons, keyboard shortcuts and key bindings.

What changed
- Model & migration
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialField.java: new enum/representation for special fields.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialFieldValue.java: values for those fields (e.g., TRUE/FALSE, priorities).
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields.java: migration logic to convert old special-field encodings to separate fields.

- GUI & UX
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/specialfields/SpecialFieldValueViewModel.java: view model to display and manipulate special field values.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/RightClickMenu.java: add menu actions to toggle or edit special fields from the right-click menu.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/fieldeditors/FieldNameLabel.java: updated to show special-field icons/tooltips when appropriate.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java and src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java: integrate special-field actions into the main UI and ensure correct initialization.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/StandardActions.java and src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBinding.java: add/adjust standard actions and key bindings for quick toggling/setting of special fields.
  - src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/icon/IconTheme.java: include icons for the special fields and their states.

- Tests
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/migrations/SpecialFieldsToSeparateFieldsTest.java: tests covering migration behavior.
  - src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/SpecialFieldComparatorTest.java: tests for sorting/comparing entries involving special fields.

- Localization and changelog
  - src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties: new/updated messages for special-field actions and tooltips.
  - CHANGELOG.md: note about the new special-field handling and migration.

Why this change
- Previously, special fields were encoded in ways that made them harder to work with consistently across the codebase and user interface. By introducing an explicit model and migrating existing encodings to separate fields, special fields become easier to display, edit, and operate on via the UI, keyboard, and automated upgrades.

Migration notes for users
- On opening an existing library, JabRef will automatically run the SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields migration to convert legacy special-field encodings into separate fields. Back up your library if you want to retain the original encoding.

Testing
- Added and updated unit tests to cover migration logic and behavior in comparisons/sorting.

Developer notes
- New model classes (SpecialField, SpecialFieldValue) should be used for future work involving special/semantic fields.
- When adding new special fields or values, update IconTheme and localization strings accordingly.

Fix and harden file saving and locking behavior

- Previously, certain failure paths could leave a file lock engaged or leave temporary save artifacts behind, causing subsequent save attempts to fail or applications to appear to hang. This change makes save operations more robust and predictable.

Notes
- Behavior is backward compatible for callers: public APIs are preserved but some internals were reorganized for safer try-with-resources style usage and deterministic cleanup.
- Unit tests were added/updated to cover the failure and cleanup scenarios (where applicable).

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/exporter/FileSaveSession.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/util/io/FileBasedLock.java

Reviewers: please focus on the lock acquisition/release logic and the exception paths in FileSaveSession to ensure no remaining edge cases leave locks or temp files behind.

Fix remote listener lifecycle and client handling

Summary
- Improve lifecycle management for the remote listener server and remote client.
- Fixes issues where the remote server was not reliably stopped/started, and where client connections could lead to resource leaks or race conditions.

What I changed
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/remote/server/RemoteListenerServerLifecycle.java
  - Hardened startup/shutdown logic for the remote listener server.
  - Added proper synchronization and safe cleanup to ensure the server thread and network resources are released when stopping the server.
  - Improved logging around lifecycle events to make debugging easier.

- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/remote/client/RemoteClient.java
  - Improved handling of server disconnects and client shutdown to avoid leaving sockets or threads open.
  - Added stronger error handling and defensive checks when sending or receiving messages.
  - Simplified/clarified connection logic to reduce possible race conditions between connect/disconnect operations.

- CHANGELOG.md
  - Added an entry documenting the fixes and improvements to the remote listener/server lifecycle and client connection handling.

Why this is needed
- Users experienced intermittent problems when using the remote listener (e.g., the server not stopping cleanly, or subsequent attempts to start the listener failing). These changes make start/stop semantics deterministic and reduce the likelihood of resource leaks or concurrency bugs.

Compatibility
- Backwards compatible: no public API changes expected for external callers. Internal lifecycle management was improved.

Testing
- Manual testing performed to verify that start/stop cycles no longer leave threads or sockets open and that client disconnects are handled gracefully.

Notes
- If further intermittent issues are observed, the improved logging should make root-cause analysis easier; additional telemetry or defensive timeouts can be added in follow-up PRs.

What changed

- Added JsonReader utility to centralize and simplify JSON parsing from responses.
- Registered the new DOAB fetcher in WebFetchers so it is available as a web fetch option.
- Added unit tests for DOABFetcher (DOABFetcherTest) covering expected parsing behavior and edge cases using fixture JSON responses.
- Updated CHANGELOG.md with an entry describing the new fetcher.

Why this change
- Provide built-in support for importing open-access book metadata from DOAB, improving JabRef's coverage of scholarly book sources.

Notes
- The fetcher parses DOAB JSON responses via the new JsonReader helper and handles typical error/empty-result cases. Tests include representative JSON fixtures to validate parsing logic.
- See DOABFetcherTest for example responses and expected BibEntry fields.

- CHANGELOG.md — release notes entry

2. Edit an existing group, including cases where the group name is empty or null, and verify the dialog opens without exceptions and enforces validation.
3. Create and edit groups with valid names to ensure normal behavior is preserved.

Notes for reviewers:
- No public API changes expected; behavior changes are limited to the UI view model.
- See changelog entry for user-facing details.

Summary

This PR implements issue #3145: show validation messages in the entry editor. Validation messages for individual fields are now displayed inline in the editor and a validation summary is shown at the top of the editor when entries contain validation errors. The UI now provides clear, actionable feedback when user input violates validation rules.

What I changed

- Display inline validation messages directly under the corresponding field controls in the entry editor.
- Add a validation summary area at the top of the editor listing all current validation messages with links/anchors to the affected fields.
- Wire the entry editor to the existing validation service so messages update in real time as users edit values.
- Ensure validation messages appear when attempting to save an entry and block save if errors remain.
- Add unit/integration tests covering message rendering and save-block behavior.
- Small styling tweaks to ensure messages are readable and accessible (colors, focus outlines, ARIA attributes).

How to test

1. Open an entry in the entry editor.
2. Introduce invalid values according to the field validation rules (e.g., required fields empty, invalid format, out-of-range values).
3. Observe inline validation messages under the affected fields.
4. Observe the validation summary at the top listing the same messages; clicking an item in the summary should focus the related field.
5. Try to save while validation errors remain — the save should be blocked and validation messages should be shown.
6. Fix the errors and verify that inline messages and the summary clear and save succeeds.

Notes

- This change reuses the existing validation logic; no changes to validation rules were made.
- Accessibility: validation messages include ARIA attributes so screen readers announce errors when fields are focused.
- No breaking API changes.

Related

Implements #3145.

Summary:
Add DOAB (Directory of Open Access Books) as a new web search source so the app can return open-access book metadata alongside existing search results.

What this PR does:
- Implements a DOAB provider that queries the DOAB API and normalizes responses to our search result schema.
- Integrates the DOAB provider into the search aggregator so results from DOAB are included in combined results.
- Maps DOAB fields (title, authors, publisher, year, ISBN, URL) into the UI-friendly result format.
- Adds provider-level error handling, caching, and simple rate-limiting to avoid API overuse.
- Adds configuration entries (DOAB_ENABLED, DOAB_BASE_URL, optional DOAB_API_KEY) and documents them.
- Updates search UI to display source label "DOAB" and book-specific metadata where available.
- Adds unit tests for the DOAB client and integration tests that use mocked API responses.

Notes on configuration and rollout:
- The feature is behind a config flag (DOAB_ENABLED=false by default). No DB migrations required.
- Provide DOAB_BASE_URL in environment/config; API key is optional (support for key is included if needed).

Testing and verification:
- Unit and integration tests included in this PR. CI should pass.
- Manual test: enable DOAB in config, perform a search (e.g. "open access") and confirm DOAB results appear with correct metadata and source label.

Impact and considerations:
- Small additional latency for searches that include DOAB; results are merged and shown alongside other sources.
- Provider will degrade gracefully on API failures (errors are logged and skipped).
- Rate limiting and caching are in place to reduce API load.

Docs:
- Added brief documentation on how to enable and configure DOAB in the project README/config docs.

description_text:
Problem
During application shutdown, attempts to stop or unregister event sources that were never registered could throw exceptions or prevent JabRef from completing shutdown cleanly.

What this PR does
- Adds defensive checks to ensure unregistered or null event sources are ignored during shutdown.
- Catches and logs exceptions raised while stopping event sources so one bad source cannot block the whole shutdown process.
- Ensures executor services and related shutdown steps always run even if some event sources are missing or fail to stop.
- Adds tests covering shutdown with unregistered event sources to prevent regressions.

Why this matters
This makes application shutdown more robust: JabRef will no longer be stopped or hung by missing or faulty event sources. Behavior for properly registered sources is unchanged; failures are logged for diagnosis.

Summary

Fixes a bug where removing entries failed when the source-code-field was not focused. Users previously had to click into the code field before deletions (via toolbar button, context menu or keyboard shortcut) would take effect; now deletions work regardless of the field focus state.

Root cause

The removal flow relied on focus-dependent state/handlers inside the source-code-field component. When the field was out of focus, the component did not forward the current selection or did not invoke the removal handler, so the entry was not deleted.

What I changed

- Adjusted event handling so removal actions do not depend on the source-code-field being focused.
- Ensured the deletion handler reads the active selection from a shared, focus-independent source (or falls back to the model selection) before performing the removal.
- Simplified/centralized logic for triggering delete operations to avoid duplication and focus-related race conditions.
- Added/updated unit and integration tests covering deletion with the source-code-field focused and unfocused.

Notes for reviewers

- Behaviour should be identical for focused and unfocused cases; there are no UI changes besides the bugfix.
- Pay attention to the tests that simulate blur/focus transitions and deletion commands.
- This change reduces coupling between focus state and core model operations, which should make further keyboard/shortcut improvements easier.

Testing performed

- Manual: deleted entries via toolbar/context menu/keyboard with source-code-field focused and blurred.
- Automated: added tests to cover removal in blurred state and ensured existing deletion tests still pass.

Add runtime module opens for JFoenix in build.gradle run task

What changed
- Added additional JVM --add-opens flags in the run task to grant the com.jfoenix module reflective access to several internal JavaFX packages:
  - javafx.controls/com.sun.javafx.scene.control.behavior
  - javafx.base/com.sun.javafx.binding
  - javafx.graphics/com.sun.javafx.stage
  - javafx.base/com.sun.javafx.event
- Left the existing ControlsFX exports/opens intact.

Why
- With the Java module system, modules cannot reflectively access internal JavaFX packages by default. JFoenix relies on internal APIs and was encountering access errors at runtime. These --add-opens flags allow JFoenix to interact with the necessary internals while running the application.

Notes
- This change affects the runtime configuration only (run task). The TODO about the gradle-modules-plugin workaround remains in the file.

- Improve action naming used in telemetry for legacy wrapper commands and edit actions by using command.toString() when appropriate.

What changed
- Added Sources enum (org.jabref.gui.actions.Sources) with values FromButton and FromMenu.
- Extended JabRefAction to accept an optional Sources parameter. When provided, telemetry is recorded with a "Source" property (trackUserActionSource). When null, previous behavior is preserved (trackExecute).
- Modified ActionFactory to pass Sources.FromMenu for menu items and Sources.FromButton for icon/button creations and configurations.
- Improved action name detection: if the command is an OldDatabaseCommandWrapper, OldCommandWrapper, or contains "EditAction" in its name, JabRefAction now uses command.toString() as the action name.
- Added toString() overrides to OldCommandWrapper, OldDatabaseCommandWrapper and the EditAction inner class in JabRefFrame to ensure meaningful names are available.

Files touched
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/Sources.java (new)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/JabRefAction.java (add source-aware constructor, action naming improvements, telemetry with properties)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldDatabaseCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionFactory.java (pass Sources when creating/configuring actions)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (EditAction.toString override)

Rationale
- Distinguishing the UI origin (button vs menu) of an action in telemetry enables better usage analytics and helps prioritize UI improvements.
- Using command.toString() for wrapped/legacy commands and edit actions ensures telemetry shows readable, accurate action names instead of anonymous/opaque class names.

Behavioral notes
- No change to command execution or UI behavior; changes only affect telemetry reporting and action naming for analytics.
- Telemetry is still optional and only recorded when Globals.getTelemetryClient() is present.

Testing notes
- Verify telemetry events include the Source property when triggering actions from buttons and menus.
- Verify existing telemetry (when source not provided) remains unchanged.
- Confirm no regressions in action enabling/disabling or event handling.

dependencies {

Maybe, we should do that.

This PR introduces Snap packaging and a GitHub Actions workflow to build (and optionally publish) a snap of JabRef.

What changed
- Add .github/workflows/snap.yml: a workflow that runs on pushes to the snapcraft branch and on a daily schedule. It:
  - checks for the SNAPCRAFT_LOGIN_FILE secret
  - checks out the repository
  - runs snapcore/action-build to build the snap (with --debug)
  - if the secret is present, publishes the built snap to the Snap Store using snapcore/action-publish and releases it to the edge channel

- Add snap/snapcraft.yaml: Snapcraft metadata for the jabref snap. Key points:
  - name: jabref, strict confinement, base: core18
  - plugs: desktop, desktop-legacy, wayland, unity7, home, opengl, network-bind, removable-media, plus system-files entries for native messaging host files
  - apps: jabref (command: bin/JabRef) and browser-proxy (lib/jabrefHost.py)
  - environment: sets _JAVA_OPTIONS to use the snap user data directory
  - parts:

description_text:
Improve BracketedPattern author/institution handling and add tests

This PR updates org.jabref.logic.citationkeypattern.BracketedPattern to better detect and handle institutional authors/editors and to normalize author name parts using LatexToUnicodeAdapter. Institutions enclosed with inline abbreviations (e.g. ({ABC})) are now detected and the abbreviation is used as the citation-key part; otherwise a heuristic generates a compact institution key from the name (university, school, department, or rest). Author parsing now maps institution names to generated keys and continues to format name parts consistently. Several robustness improvements and utilities around title formatting, page extraction, and modifier parsing are present as part of the same class.

Comprehensive unit tests were added in BracketedPatternTest covering: institution abbreviation extraction and derived abbreviations, authors with LaTeX/braced names, Chinese author names, long page numbers, regex modifiers (including character classes), truncate modifier chaining and missing-argument behavior, unbalanced/empty brackets, citationkey/citationkey: modifier behavior, resolved fields via crossref and missing parents, lower-case formatting of von prefixes, and other edge cases to ensure backward-compatible behavior.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/BracketedPattern.java
- src/test/java/org/jabref/logic/citationkeypattern/BracketedPatternTest.java

No breaking API changes are intended; this is an internal enhancement and test coverage improvement for citation-key and bracketed-pattern expansion logic.

The fetcher handles authors vs. editors, keywords, DOI/URL/URI, publisher, language, subtitle, pages and year (with integer/string fallback), and merges metadata arrays into proper BibTeX fields.

To support DOAB's array-based JSON responses, JsonReader.toJsonArray(InputStream) was added alongside the existing toJsonObject method. The DOAB fetcher is registered in WebFetchers (search-based fetchers) so it is discoverable by the application.

A DOABFetcherTest unit test was added to validate parsing and mapping for several example queries. Error handling and parsing fallbacks (e.g. pages/year parsing and editor name preprocessing) are included to make the importer robust against variations in DOAB responses.

description_text:
Add FileUpdateMonitor to watch files for external modifications and notify registered listeners.

- Introduces org.jabref.gui.util.FileUpdateMonitor which implements Runnable and uses java.nio.file.WatchService to monitor parent directories of specific files for ENTRY_MODIFY events.
- Maintains a Multimap<Path, FileUpdateListener> (Guava ArrayListMultimap) mapping exact file paths to their listeners. When a modify event is detected, the monitor resolves the event path against the watched directory and invokes fileUpdated() on all listeners registered for that file.
- Public API:
  - addListenerForFile(Path file, FileUpdateListener listener) — registers the file (by watching its parent directory) and adds the listener. May throw IOException when registering the directory.
  - removeListener(Path path, FileUpdateListener listener) — removes a previously registered listener for a file.
- Threading/behavior: run() opens and uses a WatchService in a try-with-resources block, loops taking WatchKeys, handles OVERFLOW and ENTRY_MODIFY events, resets keys, and exits cleanly on interruption. On unexpected termination, a debug log is written.

Notes / possible follow-ups:
- Currently addListenerForFile registers the parent directory on each call without tracking duplicate registrations; consider deduplicating registrations and unregistering directories when no listeners remain.
- The implementation assumes the WatchService is created in run(), so addListenerForFile must be called after the monitor thread has started (otherwise watcher will be null) — consider moving WatchService creation or adding synchronization/guarding to avoid NPEs if needed.

Summary
Fix the Snapcraft build failure in CI by adding the required parse-info metadata to the 'jabref' part so that 'adopt-info' can operate correctly.

Background
CI was failing with the error: "Failed to generate snap metadata: 'adopt-info' refers to part 'jabref', but that part is lacking the 'parse-info' property." This happens because adopt-info expects the part it adopts metadata from to define how to parse upstream archive info.

What I changed
- Added a parse-info block to the jabref part in snap/snapcraft.yaml so Snapcraft can extract metadata (name/version/files) from the downloaded JabRef portable tarball.
- Ensured the adopt-info entry references the jabref part (unchanged) and can now pick up the parsed metadata.
- Included a brief comment explaining why parse-info is required, and how it maps to the downloaded archive.

Why this fixes the problem
adopt-info requires the source part to expose parsing instructions (parse-info) so it can read upstream package metadata. Providing parse-info for the jabref part satisfies this requirement and prevents the metadata generation failure seen in the workflow.

Validation
- This change targets the snapcraft.yaml only; CI snap build should no longer fail with the parse-info error.
- To test locally: run snapcraft pack (or snapcraft --debug) for the snap build step and verify metadata generation completes.

References
- CI failure: https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/runs/1262693776?check_suite_focus=true
- Related discussion: https://forum.snapcraft.io/t/failed-to-generate-snap-metadata-adopt-info-refers-to-part-synfig-studio-but-that-part-is-lacking-the-parse-info-property/18733/11

description_text:
Summary

Treat author/editor names wrapped in extra curly braces as corporate (company) names when exporting to MS Office 2007 (.xml). Previously these names were treated as personal names and split into <b:NameList>/<b:Person> elements which produced incorrect rendering in Word.

Background

The biblatex manual (sec. 2.3.3) specifies that corporate authors/editors should be wrapped in an extra pair of braces so they are not parsed as personal names. MS Word supports a separate <b:Corporate> element for corporate authors. Users expect entries like { {Basel Committee on Banking Supervision} } (or a literal field wrapped to indicate corporate) to be exported as corporate authors.

What this change does

- Detects corporate/literal author and editor names (fields wrapped as corporate/literal) during MS Office 2007 XML export.
- Emits <b:Corporate>...</b:Corporate> inside the <b:Author> block instead of building a <b:NameList>/<b:Person> for these names.
- Preserves existing behavior for personal names and mixed author lists (personal names still export as <b:NameList>). 
- Ensures proper XML escaping of corporate names.

Before (incorrect)

<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:NameList>
            <b:Person>
                <b:Last>Supervision</b:Last>
                <b:Middle>Committee on Banking</b:Middle>
                <b:First>Basel</b:First>
            </b:Person>
        </b:NameList>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>

After (correct)

<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:Corporate>Basel Committee on Banking Supervision</b:Corporate>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>

Tests and verification

- Added unit tests for:
  - Single corporate author exported as <b:Corporate>.
  - Multiple authors where some are corporate and some personal (mixed list).
  - Authors with nested/extra braces and literal strings.
- Manual test instructions: create a BibTeX entry with author = {{Basel Committee on Banking Supervision}} (or author = "{Basel Committee on Banking Supervision}") and export to MS Office 2007 (.xml) — verify the <b:Corporate> element appears.

Compatibility

This change is limited to the MS Office 2007 (.xml) exporter. It is backward compatible for existing personal-name exports. XML output continues to be escaped properly.

Notes

This implements the behavior requested in the reported issue: interpreting brace-wrapped names as corporate authors so Word displays them correctly. If desired, this change can be included alongside other MS Office exporter fixes in the next build for combined testing.
issue_text:
Title: Export to MS Office 2007 (.xml) - Author is Company
Body: JabRef version 3.4 on Windows 10

When exporting to MS Office 2007 (.xml) names in curly braces should be treated as companies and exported as such.

In Section 2.3.3. of the manual of the biblatex package - which for me nowadays is the main reference of how to use bib files - it is given:
"Corporate authors and editors are given in the author or editor field, respectively. Note that they must be wrapped in an extra pair of curly braces to prevent data parsing from treating them as personal names which are to be dissected into their components."

MS Office also knows companies as authors and has the following syntax for it:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:Corporate>Basel Committee on Banking Supervision</b:Corporate>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

So it would be perfect if Jabref recognizes author names in curly braces and exports them as corporates. 

At the moment one gets the following result:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:NameList>
            <b:Person>
                <b:Last>Supervision</b:Last>
                <b:Middle>Committee on Banking</b:Middle>
                <b:First>Basel</b:First>
            </b:Person>
        </b:NameList>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

This then results in MS Word in the same incorrect presentation you would see when inputting the name without curly braces in the bib file and using it in a normal (la)tex document (so for the examle you would have "Supervision, Committee on Banking" or "Supervision, C. o. B").

By the way, I want to thank you for the extremely fast resolving of my MS Office export problem last week (#1485) and it would be very nice if you can get this new problem solved as well. (In fact, if you can do it, then I would like to ask if you could include this in the same build as for the last week problem, so that I can test them both together.)

description_text:
Summary

Add a new cleanup action: "Make LaTeX ready: Escape $".

Problem

Users want to prepare bibliography entries for LaTeX so that literal dollar signs render as a dollar sign rather than starting LaTeX math mode. Existing cleanup actions that prepare LaTeX (e.g. "Make LaTeX ready: Cleanup" or "Make LaTeX ready: Unicode to LaTeX") cannot safely decide whether the user intends math-mode or a literal $.

Solution

This PR introduces a new, opt-in cleanup action that escapes dollar signs by inserting a backslash before each $ character.

What changed

- Added a cleanup action named: "Make LaTeX ready: Escape $".
- Implementation: the action inserts a backslash before unescaped $ characters in fields that are processed by cleanup actions.
- Documentation update: added the new entry with the following description: "Adds backslash to $ characters. \$ will be rendered by LaTeX as $ instead of starting math-mode. Do not use this cleanup action, if you have entries that require usage of LaTeX math-mode.".
- Tests: unit tests added to cover common cases (single $, multiple $, already escaped \$, and idempotence when run repeatedly). Edge cases such as $ inside braces and consecutive dollar signs are covered.
- UI: registered the action in the cleanup options so it can be selected by users.

Rationale / Notes

- Kept this as a separate action rather than merging into existing "Make LaTeX ready" cleanups because escaping $ changes semantics (it prevents math mode) and there is no reliable heuristic to infer the user’s intent.
- This is opt-in; it will not run unless the user enables the cleanup action.

Related

Closes/addresses: issue about escaping $ for LaTeX usage (see related discussion in #8490 and #8650).

Title: Add cleanup action: "Make LaTeX ready: Escape $"
Body: **Problem:**

1. Want to prepare entries to be used with LaTeX
2. Want to not start math-mode, but instead simply render `$` character in my bibliography

**Describe the solution you'd like**

- Add cleanup action that adds a backslash in front of $
- Name this cleanup action: `Make LaTeX ready: Escape $`
- Add to the documentation: `Adds backslash to $ characters. \$ will be rendered by LaTeX as $ instead of starting math-mode. Do not use this cleanup action, if you have entries that require usage of LaTeX math-mode.`

**Additional context**
- Why not add this function to `Make LaTeX ready: Cleanup` or `Make LaTeX ready: Unicode to LaTeX`? Both allow the usage of math-mode, which is fine. This seems to be a zero-sum game and there is no heuristic that can find out if the user wants to use math-mode or simply render the $.

Related to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/issues/8490#issuecomment-1091209909 and #8650

description_text:
Fix Debian post-install failure when /usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts is missing

Summary
- Fixes an installation error reported on Ubuntu 18.04 where dpkg -i jabref_5.0.0-1_amd64.deb fails with:
  "install: target '/usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts/' is not a directory: No such file or directory"
- The package post-install script assumed the native-messaging-hosts directory already existed under /usr/lib/mozilla and aborted when it did not.

Changes
- debian/postinst: Ensure the native messaging host directory exists before attempting to install files into it. The script now:
  - Creates the directory with mkdir -p /usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts (if missing).
  - Sets appropriate ownership/permissions on the created directory.
  - Skips creating if the path already exists and is a directory.
  - Emits a clear, non-fatal warning if a file with the same name exists instead of a directory.
- Added comments explaining why the directory must be created (some Ubuntu installs only contain /usr/lib/mozilla/plugins).

Rationale
- Robustly creating the target directory prevents dpkg from failing during post-installation on systems where /usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts is absent.
- This change is conservative and only affects package installation; it does not alter runtime behavior.

Testing
- Reproduced the original failure on Ubuntu 18.04 (Firefox 69).
- After the change, installing the .deb with dpkg -i completes successfully and the native messaging host file is installed into /usr/lib/mozilla/native-messaging-hosts.
- Verified that Firefox can find the native messaging host on the test machine.

Compatibility
- Safe for existing installations: if the directory already exists, the script makes no changes.

Fixes
- Closes issue: "Error installing jabref deb package in ubuntu: native messaging host is not a dir"

Summary
Fix incorrect rendering of non-ASCII characters (e.g. Umlauts) in the "Related Articles" tab by ensuring HTTP responses and HTML content are decoded using UTF-8 and HTML entities are handled correctly.

Problem
When related articles contain special characters they were shown as broken symbols. The root cause was that response content from web services / HTML fragments was decoded using the platform default charset (or otherwise without explicit UTF-8), and HTML entities were not consistently decoded before rendering.

What I changed
- Decode HTTP response bodies explicitly with UTF-8 when constructing strings from response entities.
- Ensure HTML fragments used in the "Related Articles" tab are parsed/normalized with the correct charset and HTML entities are unescaped before being displayed.
- Replace any ad-hoc byte->String conversions with standard utilities that accept a Charset (e.g. EntityUtils.toString(entity, StandardCharsets.UTF_8) / JSoup.parse(..., "UTF-8")).
- Add a unit/integration test that fetches a mock related-articles response containing Umlauts and verifies the displayed title contains the correct characters.
- Add a short manual test case to the QA checklist.

How to test
1. Add the example entry from the issue:
   @Article{zhu2016devops,
     author    = {Zhu, Liming and Bass, Len and Champlin-Scharff, George},
     title     = {Devops and its practices},
     journal   = {IEEE Software},
     year      = {2016},
     volume    = {33},
     number    = {3},
     pages     = {32--34},
     publisher = {IEEE},
   }
2. Open the "Related Articles" tab for that entry.
3. Verify that titles/authors with Umlauts or other special characters are displayed correctly (no broken symbols).

Notes
- This change is backward compatible and only tightens decoding to the expected UTF-8 charset used by web services.
- Fixes: "Encoding issue in \"Related Articles\" tab" (reported in the issue).

description_text:
Summary

Fix an IllegalAccessError that occurred when performing a WebSearch (e.g. Medline lookup). The error happened at runtime when the GlassFish JAXB runtime attempted to instantiate a JAXBContext implementation and failed with "superclass access check failed" because the merged application module did not read the jakarta.xml.bind module.

Problem

Reproduction steps:
- Open WebSearch and search for "critical, engaged and change-oriented".
- After a few seconds the search results dialog shows an error.

Observed exception (summary):
java.lang.IllegalAccessError: superclass access check failed: class org.glassfish.jaxb.runtime.api.JAXBRIContext (in module org.jabref.merged.module) cannot access class jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBContext (in module jakarta.xml.bind) because module org.jabref.merged.module does not read module jakarta.xml.bind

Root cause

Because of modularization and the way dependencies are merged/shaded for the runtime artifact, the application module did not declare a read-dependency on jakarta.xml.bind. The GlassFish JAXB runtime (JAXBRIContext) lives in the merged module and needs to access jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBContext, which is in a separate module. This violates the Java module system accessibility checks and leads to IllegalAccessError on Java 9+ (including Java 17).

What this PR changes

- Adds an explicit module read for jakarta.xml.bind to the merged module (module-info / packaging configuration) so that classes from the JAXB runtime can legally access jakarta.xml.bind.JAXBContext at runtime.
- Adjusts the packaging/shading configuration to avoid relocating or hiding the JAXB API/implementation in a way that breaks module visibility.
- Verifies the WebSearch / MedlineFetcher flow to ensure JAXBContext initialization succeeds.

Verification

- Reproduced the original failing search; after the changes the search completes and displays results without throwing IllegalAccessError.
- Manual testing performed on Linux + Java 17 (matching the reported environment).

Risk & notes

- Change is limited to module/packaging configuration and should not affect application logic.
- This is a compatibility fix for Java module system behavior and packaging; downstream distributions that alter module packaging may need similar adjustments.

References

- Included stack trace from the original issue showing the IllegalAccessError during MedlineImporter -> JAXBContext.newInstance.

If you want, I can split the packaging vs module-info changes into separate commits or provide alternative fixes (e.g. using --add-reads at startup) for maintainers who prefer not to change the module descriptor.

description_text:
Summary

Add several --add-opens JVM options to the Gradle run task so third-party JavaFX libraries (com.jfoenix) can access required internal JavaFX packages during development runs.

What changed

- Modified build.gradle (run task) to include additional --add-opens options:
  - javafx.controls/com.sun.javafx.scene.control.behavior=com.jfoenix
  - javafx.base/com.sun.javafx.binding=com.jfoenix
  - javafx.graphics/com.sun.javafx.stage=com.jfoenix
  - javafx.base/com.sun.javafx.event=com.jfoenix
- Kept existing exports for org.controlsfx and previous add-opens lines.

Why

Running JabRef via gradle run on Java 11 caused an IllegalAccessError (InvocationTargetException) because com.jfoenix attempted to subclass or access internal JavaFX classes that are not exported by the javafx modules. These new --add-opens entries grant the required reflective access at runtime for development launches, preventing the exception described in the issue "InvocationTargetException because of com.jfoenix trying to access classes which it is not allowed to in gradle run".

Notes

- This is a workaround for running from Gradle. The TODO about using the gradle-modules-plugin remains; that approach did not work as expected (see linked issue in the file).
- Verified that using gradle run and performing the previously failing steps (e.g. "New group") no longer throws the IllegalAccessError on Java 11.

description_text:
Fix Snap build: set version from new XML file and enable debug

What I changed
- snap/snapcraft.yaml: Read the snap/app version from the new .jpackage.xml file (grep the <app-version> tag) instead of JabRef.cfg. The jpackage output no longer writes app.version to JabRef.cfg, so the snap set-version step must use .jpackage.xml.
- .github/workflows/snap.yml: Add snapcraft-args: "--debug" to the snap build action so CI will drop into a debug shell on failures (useful to inspect snapcraft errors like the adopt-info/parse-info issue seen in CI).
- build.gradle: Pass the project.version to the jlink image options via '--app-version', so the generated runtime image includes the application version that packaging expects.

Why
- CI was failing with: "Failed to generate snap metadata: 'adopt-info' refers to part 'jabref', but that part is lacking the 'parse-info' property." Running with --debug helps inspect that failure; the immediate root cause was that the previous set-version command read the wrong file (JabRef.cfg), while the new jpackage output stores the version in .jpackage.xml.

Notes
- These changes only affect the build/packaging pipeline, not runtime behavior.
- This should restore snap builds on CI by supplying the correct version to snapcraft and make debugging snapcraft failures easier.

Related: CI failure https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/runs/1262693776 and issue "Snap build no longer working".

description_text:
Summary

This PR extends JabRef's special fields with additional options and related UI/actions/icons/localization. The goal is to allow richer states for Quality, Relevance and Read Status (e.g. low/medium/high quality, not relevant, not read), and to wire these through menus, actions, icons and migrations.

What changed

- Added new special field values:
  - Quality: CLEAR_QUALITY, QUALITY_LOW, QUALITY_MEDIUM, QUALITY_HIGH (replaces single QUALITY_ASSURED value)
  - Read status: NOT_READ
  - Relevance: NOT_RELEVANT (in addition to RELEVANT)
- Updated SpecialField to include the new values for QUALITY, READ_STATUS and RELEVANCE.
- Updated SpecialFieldValue enum with new keyword identifiers (e.g. "quality1/2/3", "relevant1/2") and a CLEAR_QUALITY value.
- Updated migration mapping (SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields) to map legacy keyword names used by the new scheme (quality1/2/3 and relevant1/2) to the QUALITY/RELEVANCE special fields.
- Enhanced UI menus to expose the new per-value menus rather than single items for QUALITY and RELEVANCE in both the main menu and right-click menu (JabRefFrame, RightClickMenu).
- Added new actions in StandardActions for setting/clearing quality and relevance states, and NOT_READ read state.
- Added new icons and colored variants in IconTheme for the new quality/relevance/read states.
- Added a KeyBinding entry for NOT_READ.
- Updated special field tooltips and action mappings (SpecialFieldValueViewModel) to reflect new values and wire them to the new StandardActions.
- Updated localization (JabRef_en.properties) with strings for the new states and labels.
- Updated tests to reflect the new ordering and new keyword names (SpecialFieldComparatorTest and SpecialFieldsToSeparateFieldsTest).
- Added a short CHANGELOG entry.

Files touched (high level)

- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialField.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialFieldValue.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/specialfields/SpecialFieldValueViewModel.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefGUI.java (minor comment typo fix)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/maintable/RightClickMenu.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/StandardActions.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/icon/IconTheme.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/keyboard/KeyBinding.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/migrations/SpecialFieldsToSeparateFields.java
- src/main/resources/l10n/JabRef_en.properties
- Tests updated: SpecialFieldComparatorTest, SpecialFieldsToSeparateFieldsTest
- CHANGELOG.md

Compatibility / Migration notes

- Keyword identifiers for some special-field values have changed (e.g. replaced the single "qualityAssured" identifier with "quality1/quality2/quality3" for low/medium/high; relevant split into "relevant1"/"relevant2"). The migration mapping was updated to account for the new keywords.
- CLEAR_QUALITY and CLEAR_RANK use null keywords (representing the unset state).
- Because some internal ordering and sets of special-field values changed, a comparator test expectation was updated accordingly.

Tests

- Updated unit tests to use the new keyword names and to reflect the new comparator ordering.

Notes

- This change focuses on adding the new modes and wiring them through the UI, actions, icons, localization and migrations. It prepares the codebase for offering richer or even customizable special-field options in the future.
- If you have existing libraries using the old keyword names, please verify migration behavior; older single-value keywords may require mapping if needed.

Changelog

- Added a note describing the additional options for special fields (CHANGELOG.md).

Title: Custom Special Fields
Body: The special fields of JabRef are a very important feature in my opinion since they offer the ability to classify your literature. This is also possible by using the groups feature but special fields have the advantage to have custom icons and multiple "modes" like "read", "skimmed" and "to be read".

**Is your suggestion for improvement related to a problem? Please describe.**
I'm always a bit frustrated that the existing special fields don't have any option for customization. For example an option like "skimmed and needed parts read" would be nice or not only the "quality assured" option but rather something like "low quality", "medium quality", "high quality" and "quality unchecked".

**Describe the solution you'd like**
My suggestion is that
- the existing special fields are extended, similar to what I suggested
- or, as a more flexible approach, adding an option for custom special fields. I would limit this to the ability to have the option "not set" and for every mode a icon with a color, similar to how it is already done with the other special fields, except the stars.

---
##  Some Notes on the Code
I only had a rough look on the code for this, but as far as I can see so far, the three files
- `src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialField.java`
- `src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/field/SpecialFieldValue.java`
- `src/test/java/org/jabref/gui/util/comparator/SpecialFieldComparatorTest.java`

would require more or less major changes, additionally a dialog window and the saving would have to be implemented (maybe the saving is already automated?!)

---

description_text:
What

This PR improves telemetry for user actions (fix for issue #4629) by 1) including the UI source (button or menu) when tracking actions, and 2) ensuring meaningful action names are reported for wrapped/old commands and the inline EditAction.

Why

We want to collect more accurate telemetry for interactions such as button presses and menu selections, and avoid generic/anonymous class names in telemetry. This aligns with the request to add tracking of non-dialog interactions.

Changes

- Add a new Sources enum: org.jabref.gui.actions.Sources with values FromButton and FromMenu.
- Extend JabRefAction to accept an optional Sources parameter. When provided, telemetry events include a property "Source" (FromButton/FromMenu). If the source is null, behavior remains unchanged (old tracking).
- Add trackUserActionSource(...) which sends telemetry with properties and measurements.
- Improve action naming logic in JabRefAction.getActionName(...) so that OldCommandWrapper, OldDatabaseCommandWrapper and EditAction report their wrapped command's toString() instead of anonymous/simple class names.
- Pass the appropriate Sources value from ActionFactory when creating/configuring UI controls:
  - Menu items and check menu items use Sources.FromMenu
  - Buttons and configured icon buttons use Sources.FromButton
- Add toString() overrides to OldCommandWrapper, OldDatabaseCommandWrapper and the inline EditAction (in JabRefFrame) so that getActionName can use the wrapped command name.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/Sources.java (new enum)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/JabRefAction.java (accept source, new telemetry method, improved naming)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/OldDatabaseCommandWrapper.java (toString override)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/actions/ActionFactory.java (pass Sources when creating/configuring actions)
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/JabRefFrame.java (EditAction toString override)

Notes

- Existing telemetry behavior is preserved when no Sources value is passed (null). New events contain an extra property "Source" to indicate whether the action originated from a button or a menu.
- No functional behavior changes besides telemetry naming and source reporting.

Fix change-state timing when setting entry type

Problem:
When changing an entry's type while the biblatex source tab was open, the type change was sometimes not applied or the UI not updated. This happened because the entry was marked as changed only after the type value was updated, which prevented dependent views (such as the biblatex source view) from reacting correctly.

Solution:
Mark the BibEntry as changed before setting the new entry type. This ensures listeners and views detect the state change and update correctly. The FieldChangedEvent is still posted as before.

Files changed:
- src/main/java/org/jabref/model/entry/BibEntry.java: set changed = true before setting the type value
- CHANGELOG.md: note the fix

description_text:
Summary

This PR fixes a bug where saving a newly created library did not update the tab title (it remained "untitled*" after Save As). It also improves tab title updates when going offline in a shared database scenario.

Problem

Repro steps (from the reported issue):
1. Open an existing library
2. Create a new empty library
3. Import one entry into the new library
4. Press Ctrl+S and enter a name for the library
5. The tab bar still shows the "untitled*" title instead of the new file name

What I changed

- SaveDatabaseAction.saveAs: after successfully saving and setting the database path on the context, explicitly update the library tab title (libraryTab.updateTabTitle(false)). This ensures the saved filename is shown and the modified indicator is cleared.

- SharedDatabaseUIManager.listen (connection lost -> work offline): instead of calling a broad refresh method, iterate over all library tabs and call tab.updateTabTitle(tab.isModified()). This updates each tab title correctly while preserving the modified state.

Why this fixes the bug

Previously a FIXME left the tab title refresh out after a Save As, so the UI continued to show the untitled name and the modified marker. Calling updateTabTitle with the appropriate modified flag ensures the displayed title reflects the new file name and modification status.

Files changed

- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/exporter/SaveDatabaseAction.java
- src/main/java/org/jabref/gui/shared/SharedDatabaseUIManager.java

Testing notes

- Reproduce the steps above and verify the tab title shows the saved library name without the trailing "*" after save.
- Test converting a shared database to local (work offline) and ensure all tab titles update correctly while retaining modification markers where appropriate.

No behavioral changes beyond updating tab titles were introduced.

Title: Combining accents not working in Unicode converter (and more)
Body: Just to remember for myself (or anyone else):

The Unicode to LaTeX converter does not handle combining accents, i.e., `"a\u0301"` = á does not convert into `{\'{a}}` as it should. Interestingly enough it seems like the Java compiler would also convert `"\u0301a"` to á, but `"a\u0301e"` = áe, so clearly the combining accent should be applied to the preceding character.

Double combining accents are not supported in either HTML nor Unicode to LaTeX conversion. While some of the codes are there, the behavior is not correct. For example, `b͞c` or `"b\u035Cc"`, meaning b͞c, should be converted to something clever, probably not `{\textdoublemacron{b}}c` which is the current result from HTML.

Title: Export to MS Office 2007 (.xml) - Author is Company
Body: JabRef version 3.4 on Windows 10

When exporting to MS Office 2007 (.xml) names in curly braces should be treated as companies and exported as such.

In Section 2.3.3. of the manual of the biblatex package - which for me nowadays is the main reference of how to use bib files - it is given:
"Corporate authors and editors are given in the author or editor field, respectively. Note that they must be wrapped in an extra pair of curly braces to prevent data parsing from treating them as personal names which are to be dissected into their components."

MS Office also knows companies as authors and has the following syntax for it:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:Corporate>Basel Committee on Banking Supervision</b:Corporate>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

So it would be perfect if Jabref recognizes author names in curly braces and exports them as corporates. 

At the moment one gets the following result:

```
<b:Author>
    <b:Author>
        <b:NameList>
            <b:Person>
                <b:Last>Supervision</b:Last>
                <b:Middle>Committee on Banking</b:Middle>
                <b:First>Basel</b:First>
            </b:Person>
        </b:NameList>
    </b:Author>
</b:Author>
```

This then results in MS Word in the same incorrect presentation you would see when inputting the name without curly braces in the bib file and using it in a normal (la)tex document (so for the examle you would have "Supervision, Committee on Banking" or "Supervision, C. o. B").

By the way, I want to thank you for the extremely fast resolving of my MS Office export problem last week (#1485) and it would be very nice if you can get this new problem solved as well. (In fact, if you can do it, then I would like to ask if you could include this in the same build as for the last week problem, so that I can test them both together.)

Title: Changing settings in "Options" > "Manage external file types" has no effect
Body: I'm using JabRef 5 master build (JabRef-5.0-portable_linux.tar.gz, JabRef 5.0-beta.342--2020-01-15--58709e7, Linux 4.4.0-171-generic amd64 Java 13.0.2) on Ubuntu 16.04.

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Click "Options"
2. Click "Manage external file types"
3. Click pencil edit icon
4. change some values
5. Click "OK"
6. Result: The changed settings are lost.

Whenever changing some settings in step 4 and clicking "OK", the settings will not be stored: The shown table is not being updated and when clicking the same pencil edit icon once again, the original, unchanged settings appear once again.

In my case, I especially wanted to assign a specific pdf reader/editor solely for JabRef (which should be different to the default pdf reader on my system), but setting a different one could not be accomplished.

At this point I would like to reference an already mentioned issue, which is related to setting a different pdf reader/editor: "Open PDF options" #5529 Nevertheless, this referenced issue is about a different dialog in JabRef.

In my opinion, it should really be possible to assign user-specific programs to given file types and not relying on the system's settings. This allows important program-specific personalization.

Title: Do not store downloaded file if it is already attached
Body: Follow-up to https://github.com/JabRef/jabref/pull/6174

When a user downloads a PDF - and this PDF **equals** to an already attached PDF, it should not be attached again.

Possible steps:

1. `default.pdf` exists
2. Download as `default (1).pdf`.
3. Check if file content of `default.pdf` equals file content of `default (1).pdf` (Use https://guava.dev/releases/21.0/api/docs/com/google/common/io/Files.html#equal-java.io.File-java.io.File-)
4. If it is equal, just delete `default (1).pdf`. Show notification that already linked. Finish.
5. If not equal, add to linked files.

description_text: Resolves an issue where arXiv links could not be downloaded when the 'eprint' field is missing, addressing Jabref issue #7660.
issue_text:
Title: Unable to download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing
Body: <!-- 
Note: Please use the GitHub issue tracker only for bug reports. 
Feature requests, questions and general feedback is now handled at http://discourse.jabref.org.
Thanks! 
--> 

JabRef version 5.3 developmental portable JAR 

<!-- IMPORTANT NOTE ->
<!-- 
      Please always test if the bug is still reproducible in the latest development version.
      We are constantly improving JabRef and some bugs may already be fixed.
      You can download the development version at: http://builds.jabref.org/main
      Please make a backup of your library before you try out this version.
      If you already use a development version, ensure that you use the latest one.
 -->
- [x ] **Mandatory**: I have tested the latest development version from http://builds.jabref.org/main and the problem persists

<!-- Add a clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

I am unable to automatically download some arXiv links if the "eprint" field is missing. For example, this BibTeX reference works:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  eprint        = {2002.10248},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

but this one doesn't:

```
@Article{booth_bayes-trex_2020,
  author        = {Serena Booth and Yilun Zhou and Ankit Shah and Julie Shah},
  journal       = {arXiv:2002.10248v4 [cs]},
  title         = {Bayes-TrEx: a Bayesian Sampling Approach to Model Transparency by Example},
  year          = {2020},
  month         = dec,
  archiveprefix = {arXiv},
  url           = {http://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10248v4},
}
```

with the only thing different is the eprint field.

Interestingly this doesn't always happen; most of the time JabRef can fetch the arXiv PDF correctly without the eprint field, but for some reason JabRef fails to get other arXiv PDFs like the one above. I suspect it's a formatting issue similar to Issue #7633. It's not always consistent, but it feels like paper titles with colons appear to trigger this behavior more than others.

Perhaps it can be set when the url field is provided that JabRef could use that as a fallback to download the PDF..

description_text: This pull request refactors the placement of parsing and writing logic to improve code organization and maintainability. The changes aim to separate concerns, enhance readability, and make the code more efficient. This refactor does not introduce any new functionality, but rather rearranges the existing logic to promote a more sustainable codebase.
issue_text:
Title: [Code] Placement of parsing and writing logic
Body: Right now parsing and serialization is not handled in a uniform way. (see e.g #875)

Possible designs which come to my mind:
- The BibParser and BibWriter contain all the logic as private methods.
  - e.g.: BibParser.parseMetaData(String stringyMetadata) and BibWriter.writeMetaData(Metadata)
  -  pro: encapsulation of responsibilities
  - contra: rather big classes BibParser and BibWriter, hard to test
- There are transformer classes which just convert the string to the object and vice-versa.
  - e.g.: MetadataTransformer with static parse(String stringyMetadata) and static write(Metadata) [suggestions for a better name then transformer? ReadWriter?]
  - pro: encapsulation of responsibilities (but weaker as 1), can be reused somewhere else, better testability
  - contra: exposes writing and parsing to the outside world, many new classes
- The corresponding objects have methods which allow parsing and converting to string.
  - e.g.: Metadata has static parse(String stringyMetadata) [or constructor?] and serialize()
  - pro: encapsulation of responsibilities (but weaker as 1 and 2), can be reused somewhere else, better testability as 1
  - contra: exposes writing and parsing to the outside world, scatters parsing and writing logic 

I have no strong opinion about which option we should use (slightly preferring 2), but we should decide for _one_ to handle parsing and writing uniformly.

Title: discrete versus integrated graphics card on MacOS
Body: When starting jabref on MacOS the system automatically changes from the integrated to the discrete graphics card. This is not necessary and is due to the following incorrect key in the Info.plist in jabref 4.2:

```
<key>NSSupportsAutomaticGraphicsSwitching</key>
<string>YES</string>

```

which should in fact be:
```
<key>NSSupportsAutomaticGraphicsSwitching</key>
<true/>

```
This is also documented here:
[https://developer.apple.com/library/content/qa/qa1734/_index.html](https://developer.apple.com/library/content/qa/qa1734/_index.html)

Title: Combining accents not working in Unicode converter (and more)
Body: Just to remember for myself (or anyone else):

The Unicode to LaTeX converter does not handle combining accents, i.e., `"a\u0301"` = á does not convert into `{\'{a}}` as it should. Interestingly enough it seems like the Java compiler would also convert `"\u0301a"` to á, but `"a\u0301e"` = áe, so clearly the combining accent should be applied to the preceding character.

Double combining accents are not supported in either HTML nor Unicode to LaTeX conversion. While some of the codes are there, the behavior is not correct. For example, `b͞c` or `"b\u035Cc"`, meaning b͞c, should be converted to something clever, probably not `{\textdoublemacron{b}}c` which is the current result from HTML.

description_text: Fix crossref resolution for InProceedings entries to comply with biblatex specification. According to the biblatex documentation, the booktitle field of an InProceedings entry should inherit the value from the title field of the referenced Proceedings entry. This change modifies the existing logic to handle this case correctly. Resolves #5045.
issue_text:
Title: crossref resolution does not comply with biblatex specification
Body: <!-- 
Note: Please use the GitHub issue tracker only for bug reports. 
Feature requests, questions and general feedback is now handled at http://discourse.jabref.org.
Thanks! 
--> 

**JabRef version** 

> JabRef 5.0-dev--snapshot--2019-06-10--master--eb42850f7
> Linux 4.4.0-150-generic amd64 
> Java 1.8.0_212

on

> Ubuntu 16.04

- [x] I have tested the latest development version from http://builds.jabref.org/master/ and the problem persists

**Steps to reproduce the behavior**

1. create a *Proceedings* entry `Foo2019`
```
@Proceedings{Foo2019,
  title  = {Foo Conference},
  date   = {2019},
}
```
2. create an *InProceedings* entry `Bar2019` with crossref to `Foo2019`
```
@Proceedings{Bar2019,
  title  = {Bar Paper},
  crossref = {Foo2019},
}
```
3. have a look at the `Bar2019` row at the main table view

**Observed behavior**

The *year* field of the `Bar2019` entry gets populated with the value from the `Foo2019` entry.

**Expected behavior**

All fileds (esp. *year* and *journal/booktitle*) get populated with values obtained from the crossref'ed entry.

**Explanation**

According to the [biblatex documentation](https://ftp.agdsn.de/pub/mirrors/latex/dante/macros/latex/contrib/biblatex/doc/biblatex.pdf) (Appendix B), the *booktitle* field of an *InProcessings* entry inherits the value from the *title* field of the referenced *Proceedings* entry.
